# coreboot fixtures

`romstage.lzma` is the stage body for the CBFS fixtures in
`tests/coreboot.rs` and `web/tests/coreboot.test.mjs`. Every FMAP image,
CBFS region and legacy ROM in those tests is built in the test from the
documented wire layout; only this LZMA stream needs an external encoder.
No coreboot or Chrome OS firmware is redistributed.

## Payload

The input is `tests/fixtures/transforms/aarch64.text.bin` (6384 B,
SHA-256 `813ee8804e2c0f2aa98e447082bdab719977bc3a1c263fda8392e4d9d044979b`):
AArch64 machine code compiled from the synthetic `sample.c`, unlinked (see
`tests/fixtures/transforms/README.md`). It stands in for a stage's flat
program image; it is not a coreboot stage.

## Generator and commands

Generated on 2026-10-12, macOS AArch64, with XZ Utils 5.8.2 and Python
3.14.7, by `generate.sh`, and regenerated byte for byte (same SHA-256) with
the same tools on 2026-10-13:

```sh
xz --format=lzma --lzma1=preset=9,dict=64KiB -c ../transforms/aarch64.text.bin > romstage.lzma
```

xz writes LZMA-alone with an unknown decoded size (all ones) and an end
marker. cbfstool records the decoded size instead, so `generate.sh` then
writes the input length (6384) as the little-endian 64-bit size field at
bytes 5-12. The end marker stays in the stream; the decoder stops at the
recorded size.
